steps.title: Hold a key and drag
steps.text: Select files in File Explorer or on the desktop and drag them with Ctrl held down, or any modifier key you choose.

steps.title: Drop on a format
steps.text: A donut of the formats that fit those files opens at your cursor. Move onto one and let go.

steps.title: Done, next to the original
steps.text: A progress ring counts up and the new files appear beside the originals. Prefer menus? Right-click and choose Convert with Filee.

items.title: A donut at your cursor
items.text: The formats appear where you already are, with no app window in the way. A modifier key, mouse button, hold gesture or keyboard shortcut opens it. One slice can hold a group of presets.

items.title: {formatCount} formats, one gesture
items.text: Images, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HWP, e-books, video, audio, subtitles, data files, 3D models, archives, CAD drawings and fonts. Filee plans the route between formats automatically.

items.title: No Office needed
items.text: Word, Excel and PowerPoint files convert without Microsoft Office or LibreOffice, and HWP without Hancom Office. Filee doesn't use Office or Hancom Office even when they are installed.

items.title: Batch conversion
items.text: Drop 1 file or 100. They're converted in parallel, a failure never stops the rest, and presets can merge everything into one PDF or one ZIP.

items.title: 100% on your PC
items.text: Nothing is uploaded. Filee works offline, so private documents, photos and recordings never leave your computer.

items.title: Right where you work
items.text: The drag gesture, Convert with Filee in the right-click menu (on Windows 11 also in the top-level menu), Send To, a keyboard shortcut or the drop zone in the main window.

items.title: Presets per file type
items.text: Quality, resizing, rotate and flip, DPI, grayscale, metadata, background removal, Trace to SVG, TIFF compression, ICO sizes, PDF merge, split, page ranges, compression and one long image, 720p, HEVC and AV1 video, hardware encoding, every frame as pictures, MP3 bitrate, output folder, file names and the original file dates.

items.title: Engines on demand
items.text: Large engines are optional. Tick them in the installer or download them in the app later: {engineNames}. Filee shows their versions, download speed and time left. Already have FFmpeg, calibre or Pandoc? Filee finds them and skips the download.

items.title: Free and open source
items.text: MIT licensed, no ads, no account. In English, Korean, Simplified Chinese and Polish. Filee tells you about new versions; every release lists its changes and contributors.

cli.description: Use the free filee command on Windows to convert files, folders and wildcards offline, watch folders, and script conversions with JSON output and exit codes.

setup.title: Keep it ticked in Setup
setup.text: On the options page of the Filee installer, leave **Add the "filee" command to PATH** ticked (it is on by default). Already installed? Run the latest installer again.

setup.title: Open a new terminal
setup.text: Open a new Command Prompt, PowerShell or Windows Terminal window (one that was already open doesn't see the new PATH) and run `filee version`.

setup.title: Portable or without PATH
setup.text: Everything is in the Filee folder: run `filee-cli.exe` there, or add its `cli` folder to PATH yourself. The app doesn't need to be running.

cli.quickLead: Pass file names, wildcards like `*.heic` or whole folders. Results are saved next to the originals unless you add `-o`.

commands.name: convert
commands.text: Converts files, wildcards (`*.heic`) and folders. A folder converts the files in it that Filee knows; add `-r` for its sub folders. Give either a target format or one of your presets.
options: Target format by id or extension: jpg, png, webp, pdf, docx, hwpx, mp4, mp3… (see `filee formats`)
A preset from the app, by id or by name (see `filee presets`)
Save there instead of next to the sources
Image quality for JPG, WebP, AVIF and other lossy formats
Replace existing output files (by default a number is added to the new name)
Give converted files the created and modified dates of the originals
Print the result as one JSON document, for scripts

commands.name: watch
commands.text: Converts every file that lands in the folder until you press Ctrl+C. Converted files go to a `converted` folder inside it unless you add `-o`.
options: A preset from the app, by id or by name
Also watch sub folders (their files keep the sub folder in the output)
Move each converted source to `<folder>\originals`, and convert the files already waiting there at start
How long a file must stay unchanged before it is converted (default 2)
Give converted files the created and modified dates of the originals

commands.name: formats
commands.text: Lists every format with its id and extensions, or what one format converts to, including what an optional engine would add.

commands.name: presets

commands.name: help

cli.watchLead: Let a folder convert whatever you put in it: downloads, scans, exports from other apps.
watchPoints: Files are converted once they are complete, no longer growing and not open in another program, so downloads and long copies are safe.
Temporary and hidden files (`.crdownload`, `.part`, `.tmp`, `~$` files) and formats Filee doesn't know are ignored.
Converted files go to a `converted` folder inside the watched folder, or wherever `-o` points. With `-r` files from sub folders keep their sub folder there (`2025\a.png` → `converted\2025\a.pdf`).
With `--move-originals` each converted source moves to `originals`, so the folder works like an inbox. Files already waiting there are converted at start.
cli.watchAppTitle: Or in the app, in the background
cli.watchAppText: The **Watch folders** page in Filee does the same without a terminal: add folders, pick a preset for each, and they are converted while Filee runs in the tray.
cli.scriptsLead: `--json` prints one JSON document with every file's result, and the exit code tells your script how it went.
exitCodes: Some files failed (the others were converted)
Wrong arguments, an unknown format or preset, or a missing input
notes: Same engines and presets as the app: a preset you make or change in Filee works with `--preset` right away, by id or by name.
Optional engines (FFmpeg, LibreOffice…) are installed in the app under Settings → Engines. `filee formats <format>` shows which conversions need one.
Wildcards are expanded by filee itself, so `*.heic` works in Command Prompt as well as in PowerShell. Put paths with spaces in quotes.
Nothing is uploaded and no internet is needed: files are converted on your PC, as in the app.
Messages are in English, so scripts and logs read the same on every PC.
